title: Decentralized Namespace
guidingQuestion: How do names and identities persist when platforms change?
summary: A decentralized namespace keeps human-meaningful names and identifiers portable across services, communities, and time.
humanIssue: Losing your identity when platforms change
webProblem: Usernames and identities belong to platforms

hero.headline: Your name should outlast any single app.
hero.text: Handles, domains, and display names are rented from platforms. When a service pivots, bans, or dies, the name people know you by often disappears with it.

problemStory.title: Why this matters
problemStory.scenario: A creator builds an audience under a username for a decade. The platform changes ownership, the handle is reassigned, and years of recognition evaporate overnight.

webLimitations.title: Why today's Web struggles
webLimitations.text: Namespaces are competitive moats. Each service invents its own naming scheme, so continuity depends on corporate goodwill rather than open resolution.

futureVision.title: Imagine instead
futureVision.text: People and communities control persistent names that resolve across apps, with clear delegation and revocation.
bullets: Resilient links that survive platform churn
